summary: The check:standards gate's DEFINITION OF GREEN as an explicit, machine-diffable CONTRACT (#2769, executing the #2625 contract-split ruling, fork (d), under the #2564 spec-based-programming line and the #2445 two-tier trust chain). The gate's IMPLEMENTATION — the ~3900 lines of imperative rules in scripts/check-standards.mjs + scripts/check-standards-rules.mjs — stays in the ENGINE tier (a behaviour-preserving refactor is agent-clearable). What moves here, as DATA not code, is the small set of knobs that DECIDE PASS-VS-FAIL: (1) the per-rule ENFORCEMENT flags — the *_ENFORCED booleans that decide whether a rule's finding is a hard ERROR (fails the gate) or merely a WARNING (does not), and (2) the semantic THRESHOLDS — the tunable numbers/allowed-sets a finding is measured against. The gate's meta-rule is fixed: check-standards.mjs exits non-zero iff there is at least one ERROR; WARNINGS never fail the gate. So flipping any enforcement flag from true to false, or loosening a threshold, is a REAL WEAKENING of the gate — it demotes a hard failure to advisory. Because every such knob is declared HERE and its value is pinned to the impl by the conformance suite (check-standards.conformance.test.mjs), 'did the definition of green change?' collapses to 'did this file change?' — a deterministic yes/no. COVERAGE (v2, #2786): the suite guards BOTH classes against a knob silently escaping this file — every boolean the engine exports (type-based, name-agnostic) must be an enforcement flag declared here, and every symbol in the engine's hand-maintained THRESHOLD_KNOBS registry (check-standards-rules.mjs; thresholds are heterogeneous so cannot be auto-discovered by type) must be declared here too. The one residual gap neither strategy closes: a boolean or bound INLINED at its call site, never a named export, is invisible to a coverage guard over the module's exports. This contract's basename is registered on the trust-chain POLICY tier (scripts/lib/gate-config.mjs), so a diff to it forces review:human (an agent may not clear an edit to its own leash, #2285); a behaviour-preserving impl edit that keeps the conformance suite green does not. Precedent: scripts/lib/review-policy.contract.json (#2566/#2564). Per #2564 a spec is a schema skeleton + a first-class prose layer in one artifact: the machine-checkable shape is the fields below, the MEANING is the 'description' prose on each entry. NOTE ON SINGLE-SOURCING: unlike review-policy (where the impl imports the numbers from the contract), this contract MIRRORS the impl's exported constants and the conformance suite PINS the two equal — because the #2769 scope deliberately does not edit the engine files. The guarantee is identical: the impl and the contract cannot diverge silently (divergence turns the suite red), so a weakening edit to the engine forces a matching contract edit → the policy tier → review:human.

enforcement.description: The per-rule ENFORCEMENT switches — for each rule that is enforced behind a named flag, whether its finding is emitted as a hard ERROR (fails check:standards) or suppressed/demoted to a WARNING. Each key mirrors a boolean constant exported from scripts/check-standards-rules.mjs (named in `impl`); the conformance suite asserts `value` equals that live constant, so flipping the flag in the engine without editing this file turns the suite red. Flipping any true to false is a definition-of-green weakening (a hard gate error becomes advisory) — the exact change #2625 requires a human to clear.

composeTraits.description: Whether a block's composesBehaviors entry that references an unsatisfied required trait is an ERROR. Currently WARN-FIRST (false, #937): flips to error once the deny-list is curated and false-positive-free. Raising it to true STRENGTHENS the gate; the flag exists so that flip is a deliberate, human-gated edit here.

exportShape.description: Whether contract-vs-barrel export-shape drift on a block is a hard ERROR (#927, enforced since #1206). true today — flipping to false would let a block's public export surface silently drift from its contract without failing the gate.

navActiveState.description: Whether a template that omits the required nav active-state a11y markup is a hard ERROR. true — flipping to false demotes an accessibility regression to a warning.

renderersPublish.description: Whether a renderer leaking into a published @webeverything exports map is a hard ERROR (#964). true — flipping to false would let renderers enter the published surface without failing the gate.

referenceRuntimeForms.description: Whether a serve() form outside the frozen reference-runtime catalog is a hard ERROR (#964). true — flipping to false unfreezes the ratified form set.

plugUnpluggedTest.description: Whether a plug missing either the plugged- or unplugged-mode test is a hard ERROR. true — flipping to false lets a plug ship a mode with no test.

repoLocusPrefix.description: Whether a doc reference lacking a required <repo>: locus prefix is a hard ERROR. true — flipping to false demotes an un-prefixed (silently-unmatched-by-scope-lease) locus to a warning.

blockImplDrift.description: Whether a moved/deleted FUI block implementation (contract points at a missing impl) is a hard ERROR (#926). true — flipping to false lets a block's impl vanish without failing the gate.

plugDrift.description: Whether WE↔FUI plug shared-core drift is a hard ERROR (#1309). true — flipping to false lets the WE and FUI copies of a plug's shared core diverge silently.

testOnlyExport.description: Whether an export that no non-test module imports and that its own module never references again is a hard ERROR (#2967a — the reduceLensJury 'extracted, tested, never wired' class). Currently WARN-FIRST (false), on the composeTraits precedent: a broad structural scan ships advisory until its carve-out set is confirmed false-positive-free, then flips. Raising it to true STRENGTHENS the gate.

unfencedMandate.description: Whether a build…Mandate builder that splices a parameter into instruction text with no fenceUntrusted path is a hard ERROR (#2967b, #2438's fence). true from day one, with both live call sites fixed in the same change — the rule establishes that caller-supplied text reaches a mandate unfenced, NOT that such text can steer an agent's verdict (unmeasured). Flipping to false parks a source-hygiene gate behind a warning stream.

thresholds.description: The semantic THRESHOLDS — the tunable numbers/allowed-sets a finding is measured against, extracted out of the impl. Each key mirrors a constant exported from scripts/check-standards-rules.mjs (named in `impl`); the conformance suite pins `value` equal to that live constant. These are care-level tuning knobs (loose to start, tightened from data); a loosening is a definition-of-green change and lives only here.

digestMaxWords.description: The maximum word count for a backlog item's digest (lead paragraph) before check:standards WARNS — the one-glance-selection budget. Raising it loosens the readability bar.

allowedSizes.description: The allowed values for a backlog item's `size` field (the Fibonacci rule-set). A size outside this set is a hard ERROR. Adding a value (e.g. 21) or dropping the constraint loosens what the gate accepts.

mandateFenceAllowedParams.description: The build…Mandate parameters exempt from the #2438 fence (#2967b) — CLOSED vocabularies, never caller free text: a validated lens name, round numbers, an isolation mode, the structural nouns a subject adapter supplies, and the boolean that turns the fence on. Adding a name here EXEMPTS a parameter from the gate, so it is a definition-of-green loosening and lives only in this file.

backlogKinds.description: The allowed values for a backlog item's `kind` field (#466/#487/#2691/#3567). A kind outside this set is a hard ERROR. Adding a value widens what the gate accepts as a valid backlog item shape.

backlogStatuses.description: The allowed values for a backlog item's `status` field (#375). A status outside this set is a hard ERROR. Adding a value widens the backlog's state machine without a matching workflow.

parkedReasons.description: The allowed values for a parked item's `parkedReason` field (#1392, tightened 2026-06-22). A reason outside this set is a hard ERROR — parking is not a prioritisation escape. Adding a value re-opens a soft park reason the tightening retired.

standardEntityKinds.description: The allowed entity kinds for a `<repo>:` standard reference. A kind outside this set fails to resolve as a standard entity. Adding a value widens what a doc reference can point at without a matching registry.

lifecycleStates.description: The allowed values for a standard entity's `status` (implementation-lifecycle) field. A status outside this set is a hard ERROR. Adding a value widens the lifecycle vocabulary a standard can claim.

projectTiers.description: The allowed values for a Project's `tier` field (the #portfolio-project-tiering enum). A tier outside this set — or a missing tier — is a hard ERROR. Adding a value widens the portfolio-tiering vocabulary.

capPolyfillClasses.description: The allowed values for a Capability's `polyfill` class. A value outside this set is a hard ERROR. Adding a value widens what a capability may claim about its polyfill story.

referenceRuntimeForms.description: The frozen reference-runtime `serve()` form catalog (#956), consulted only when `unfencedMandate`'s sibling flag `referenceRuntimeForms` (REFERENCE_RUNTIME_FORMS_ENFORCED) is true. A new WE-side form outside this set is a hard ERROR while enforced. Adding a value here — independent of the enforcement flag — unfreezes the ratified form set, the exact #956 escape the flag exists to close.

locusNames.description: The allowed values for a backlog item's `locus` field when `locusAuthored` is set — derived as the key set of the engine's LOCI routing table (repoPath/gateCommand/devServerProbe per locus, which are operational routing, not a gate boundary, so only the key set is governed here). A locus outside this set is a hard ERROR. Adding a value widens which repo a cross-locus item may claim without the routing table actually knowing that repo.

tierStates.description: The allowed capability-adapter tier values for a `kind: native` (default) adapter. A tier outside this set is a hard ERROR. Adding a value widens the native substrate-state vocabulary.

libraryTierStates.description: The allowed capability-adapter tier values for a `kind: library` adapter — the coverage-state vocabulary, distinct from `tierStates`. A tier outside this set is a hard ERROR. Adding a value widens what a library adapter may claim about its coverage.

maturityTriggerPattern.description: The pattern a `parkedReason: maturityGated` item's `maturityTrigger` must match (#1620) — a typed counter or named external artifact, never a date or bare prose. A `maturityTrigger` that fails this is a hard ERROR. Loosening the pattern (e.g. accepting bare prose) re-opens the soft-deferred escape #1620 closed. Compared against the live `MATURITY_TRIGGER_RE.source`, not the RegExp object.

pilotEvidenceNums.description: The backlog item ids that satisfy the #2089 forward-target-start-gate's evidence edge (docs/agent/platform-decisions.md#forward-target-start-gate) — a `polyglot-widening`-tagged item clears the gate with a `blockedBy` edge to one of these. A `polyglot-widening` item lacking this edge (and lacking a carve-out tag or its own maturityTrigger) is a hard ERROR. Adding an id here widens what counts as satisfying evidence without new adopter data.

polyglotWideningTag.description: The tag that opts a backlog item into the #2089 forward-target-start-gate (declared-over-auto-derived: the author asserts the item adds a new generation target/emit form). Renaming this constant without a matching item-tag migration would silently stop the gate from firing on every existing item still carrying the old tag string — a definition-of-green weakening by omission, not by value.

polyglotCarveoutTags.description: Tags that exempt a `polyglot-widening`-tagged item from the #2089 evidence-edge requirement — work that consumes existing emit forms and adds no new target/form. Adding a value here widens the carve-out, letting more items skip the evidence-edge gate.

strandedHashGraceSeconds.description: The in-flight grace window (#2288/#2956) a non-numeric backlog-file id on main is given before `strandedHashesOnMain` treats it as a real strand (hard ERROR) rather than the drain's own JIT-numbering commit still in flight (WARNING). Raising it demotes a genuine stranded hash to advisory for longer — a hard failure becomes silently tolerable.

pluginSharedCoreFiles.description: The plug-core files contractually required byte-identical across WE and FUI (#1304/#1350), consulted only when `plugDrift` (PLUG_DRIFT_ENFORCED) is true. Removing a file from this list stops checking its WE↔FUI parity while the flag itself stays enforced — a silent narrowing of what `plugDrift` actually covers.

webeverythingPublishedScope.description: The published-package scope `validateRenderersNotPublished` scans, consulted only when `renderersPublish` (RENDERERS_PUBLISH_ENFORCED) is true. Narrowing or renaming this prefix would silently stop scanning real `@webeverything/*` manifests for a renderer leak while the flag itself stays enforced.

moduleResolutionLockedScope.description: The importmap/alias scope `validateModuleResolutionLock` polices (#271/#274) — an entry under this prefix must resolve to the package's exports, never a raw source path; a hard ERROR when it doesn't. Narrowing this prefix exempts entries from the lock without touching the check itself.

derivedArtifactDirs.description: The directories `validateUntrackedDerivedArtifacts` (#2180) hard-errors on when they hold untracked files (a local-gate-green/CI-red trap — a fresh clone has no untracked files). Removing a directory from this list lets untracked derived artifacts accumulate there with no warning until CI reds.

playwrightContainerPinRequiredFiles.description: The workflow files `validatePlaywrightContainerPin` (#2234) requires to carry an in-lockstep `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:vX.Y.Z-jammy` container pin, hard ERROR when missing/drifted. Dropping a file from this list stops verifying its pin, silently reopening the byte-reproducibility gap the pin exists to close.

githookAllAllow.description: The comment marker that suppresses `findGitHookAllFlags`'s hard ERROR on a git-hook invocation carrying `--all` (a machine-global-tree-creation footgun on an unattended hook). Widening or emptying this marker string would let more/all invocations silently escape the check via a trivially-satisfied comment.

graduatedRefPattern.description: The `kind:slug` compact-reference pattern (#247) that opts a resolved item's `graduatedTo` value into resolution validation (unknown kind / unresolved slug — both hard ERROR). A value that fails to match is treated as free-form prose and left unvalidated by design, so NARROWING this pattern is the loosening direction here: it lets more `graduatedTo` values silently skip resolution checking. Compared against the live `GRADUATED_REF.source`, not the RegExp object.

surfaceZonePrefixes.description: The path prefixes `classifySurfacePaths` considers in-zone; a path outside them is `neutral` and simply skipped, never reaching the unclassified hard ERROR. Narrowing this list exempts more of the tree from the site/standard classification (and its unclassified-path error) entirely — the companion scope of SITE_SURFACE_MATCHERS/STANDARD_SURFACE_MATCHERS, which this registry cannot itself declare (see THRESHOLD_KNOBS' doc comment: they're arrow-function arrays, not JSON-representable).

lockPointCodeLinesThreshold.description: Half of the #2678 Fork 1 ratified lock-point composite (docs/agent/platform-decisions.md#small-file-preference) — a file this large, combined with enough queued-item scope collisions, gets flagged as a throughput lock point. Permanently WARN (never an error, never a deny, by the ratification itself), same shape as DIGEST_MAX_WORDS: raising this silently quiets the warn for ever-larger files, loosening a real budget the contract still governs even though nothing here can become a hard error.

lockPointCollisionsThreshold.description: The other half of the #2678 lock-point composite — how many queued (non-resolved) items' `scope:` must name a file before it counts as collision-heavy. Permanently WARN, same shape as DIGEST_MAX_WORDS: raising this silently quiets the warn for ever-more-contended files.

scopeBasenameMaxSuggestions.description: The #3337 basename-mismatch lint's suggestion-count ceiling — a wide top tier (more candidates than this) is treated as silence rather than a noisy suggestion list. Permanently WARN, per its own doc comment ("WARNING, NEVER AN ERROR"), same shape as DIGEST_MAX_WORDS: raising this silently quiets the warn for an ever-wider ambiguous-basename set.
